verdict.rationale: Pipecat is a voice-agent framework, so plugging in MCP servers as tool sources is a fair question for it. However, the evidence pack documents no MCP-client capability for voice agents. The only MCP mention is context-hub registering itself as an MCP server for a coding agent, which is a different role. Flows function calling is an adjacent feature, not MCP tool sourcing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my voice agent can plug in MCP servers as tool sources so one integration grants it whole toolsets mid-call
